title: Oncall handoff - Ethan Carter (Mar 04 2026)
content:
Shift summary (Mar 03 22:00 PST -> Mar 04 06:00 PST)

Quick TL;DR:
- Two small incidents: one autoscale flapping on eu-west Dedicated pool (resolved), one transient 503s from hosted-api edge in us-west (investigated, mitigated).
- No active Sev; post-shift follow-ups listed below.
- Health: overall token throughput ~normal, slight tail latency bump on long-context workloads (L2).

Active items (to pick up)
1) AUTOSCALE-FLAP-EU (JIRA-5278) - status: mitigated, monitoring
   - Symptom: dedicated GPU pool in eu-west started oscillating between scale-up and scale-down over ~45m, causing short drops in capacity and increased queue depth.
   - Root cause (likely): mis-tuned cooldown/scale-up policy interacting with sudden drop in short-lived jobs after a spike; policy triggered scale-down too aggressively.
   - Mitigation applied: manually bumped min-replicas to 2 for the pool and pinned instance group until config fix. Reverted after traffic normalized.
   - Next steps:Eng SRE follow-up to propose safer cooldowns + add hysteresis (owner: Maya). Add a smoke test for scaling cooldowns.

2) HOSTED-EDGE-503-USW (incidental) - status: monitoring
   - Symptom: short burst of 503s (~1-2m) across several edges in us-west at 03:10 UTC, correlated with a transient spike of malformed keep-alive connections from a client upstream.
   - Action taken: temporarily blacklisted offending IP range at edge LB level; traffic normalized. Raised a request with edge infra to add better connection-level metrics.
   - Follow-up: Contact edge infra (Samir) to review blacklisting policy and instrument connection error metrics (task created).

System health notes\- Redis K/V cache: no evictions beyond normal; current memory at 68% in prod-cache-01.
- KV cache hitrate: 72% overall (down ~3% vs baseline) — likely from increased long-context in requests.
- Serving runtime: a small increase in p95 and p99 token latency for model family L2 (long-ctx) observed between 01:00-03:30 UTC. Investigated model kernel metrics, no OOMs.
- Observability: one missing span on the router->runtime hop due to SDK bump; traced to rollout PR #413 in staging. Keep an eye.

Temporary procedures / quick playbook (for next 8h)
A) If you see autoscale oscillation in Dedicated pools:
   1. Check pool scaling metrics (scale events, queue depth) in Console -> Dedicated -> pool metrics.
   2. If scale events > 3 within 30m and queue depth spikes, set min-replicas +=1 (via admin console) to steady capacity.
   3. Notify infra channel (#dedicated-pools). Add comment to the JIRA ticket for the pool.
   4. Retain pinned instance group if traffic is spiky; unpin once queue depth stable for 45m.
   5. Escalate to oncall eng lead if capacity < 50% and customer-facing errors reported.
   Quick commands (kubectl/admin tooling):
     - ./tools/poolctl status --pool eu-west-dedicated-1
     - ./tools/poolctl set-min --pool eu-west-dedicated-1 --min 2

B) If hosted API 5xx spike from edge region:
   1. Check edge LB logs (edge/console) for source IPs and connection patterns.
   2. Temporarily block offending IP range at edge LB (edge infra docs, one-line command in ops-runbook).
   3. If blocking not possible, route traffic to fallback region via traffic policy.
   4. Add comment in incident channel and create a follow-up ticket for edge infra.

Known flaky/fragile things to watch\- Model L2 long-context p99 latency is sensitive to batch size and KV cache miss rate — if p99 jumps >20% investigate cache hitrate and batching config.
- The routing SDK bump (PR #413) in staging caused a missing trace span; may roll forward if not fixed.
- Occasionally see auth token refresh failures from one of the telemetry collectors — matched by small uptick in "auth.refresh.failed" alerts last week. If you see an auth cascade, restart telemetry collector: ./scripts/collector-restart.sh telemetry-usw-2

Escalation contacts\- Oncall ENG Lead: Maya Singh (pager: +1-555-0102, slack: @maya)
- Edge Infra Eng: Samir Ali (slack: @samir)
- Platform Lead (urgent): Lexi Martin (pager: +1-555-0119)
- Customer-facing support: Olivia Hu (customer-success)

Pending TODOs / follow-ups created during shift\- JIRA-5278 (autoscale cooldown) - assign to Maya for config proposal.
- Ticket: EDGE-1904 - request connection-level metrics and blacklist review (Samir).
- PR: routing-sdk#413 - monitor for fix; if not fixed after 24h, roll back to previous minor.

Notes to self / tips\- When investigating queue depth spikes, prefer the per-route histogram first (Console -> Routes -> {route} -> Queue Depth) — global pool metrics are slower to update.
- If you need to test scaling changes, use the staging pool eu-west-staging-1 and the load-generator job: ./tools/loadtest --pool eu-west-staging-1 --profile spike-10m
- Keep a copy of the ban list in /ops/edge/banlist.txt and add ephemeral blocks as comments in Slack thread for traceability.

Misc scribbles (unsorted)
- Consider adding a small safety window (5m) to dedicated pool scale-down to prevent oscillation during bursty low-latency workloads.
- Check whether the L2 family kernel selection logic has a pathological path for seq_len>32k (rare) — flag to research team.

End of handoff. Short and messy — ping me in Slack if anything is unclear.

Ethan
